prompt: Some people think that all advertising aimed at children under the age of twelve should be banned. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
A ban is the right instrument, but the usual justification for it — that advertising makes children want things — is too weak to carry the argument, since that is what advertising does to everyone and we permit it. The reason for treating children differently is narrower and a great deal stronger.

Persuasion is legitimate between parties who both know it is happening. An adult watching a commercial may well be influenced, but the influence operates through a defence: the viewer knows the source has an interest, discounts what is said accordingly, and can reasonably be held responsible for what they do next. That defence is absent in a six-year-old and only half-assembled at eleven. A message pitched at that audience does not persuade so much as install, and the transaction has no informed party on one side of it.

This is why the objection about parental responsibility misses its target. Parents are indeed the ones holding the money, but the strategy is not aimed at the purchase; it is aimed at the child, who is then deployed against the parent in a supermarket aisle. Placing the burden on families amounts to asking them to win, repeatedly and in public, an argument that has been professionally engineered for them to lose.

The real difficulty is not principle but drafting. Advertising to children is no longer a slot between cartoons. It is a character skin in a game, a cereal woven into an animated series, a video made by someone whose audience is nine, and any statute framed around intent will be complied with exactly and evaded entirely. The test has to be the audience a message actually reaches, and the liability has to sit with the brand paying for it rather than the platform carrying it.

Written that way, the ban is enforceable and I would support it without reservation. Written as a rule about television, it redirects a budget rather than reducing one.
title: Advertising aimed at young children
